subject: FluxBank incident: recovery notes, timeline, and committed mitigations
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <ops@fluxbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T14:12:00Z
Subject: Elevated latency and sporadic 503s observed this morning

Marissa / Redwood team,

We started seeing elevated request latencies for embeddings and occasional 503s against our production endpoints beginning ~13:45 UTC. Impact: multiple client-facing features experienced timeouts; estimated 6% request failure rate during the peak.

Can you confirm you are investigating and give an ETA for a status update? We have customers pinging support.

Thanks,
Oliver
Senior SRE, FluxBank

Attachments: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <ops@fluxbank.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Elevated latency and sporadic 503s observed this morning

Oliver — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We're actively triaging. Quick notes: 
- I’ve escalated to our runtime team and looped in Connor and Lauren for visibility.
- Initial telemetry shows a spike in queue depth on the autoscale controller for the region handling your requests.
- We will send an interim update within 60 minutes.

Immediate next steps (what we'll do now):
1) Increase capacity on the affected pool to reduce queueing.
2) Capture full request traces and slow queries for a 2-hour window.
3) Begin a focused log review for any scheduling/eviction events.

We’ll follow up shortly with more details and a mitigation ETA.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:05:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: initial findings from triage (do not forward)

Team — quick internal summary from the first hour of triage: 
- Root cause (preliminary): a regression in the autoscale controller logic that misclassified sustained burst traffic as ramp-downable, causing delayed pod/provisioning decisions under this workload pattern. The controller reduced effective capacity for ~8 minutes during the peak.
- Contributing factor: a recent kernel update to the GPU instances increased cold-start latency for some model variants; combined with the controller regression this amplified queue depth.
- Impact window: 2027-04-10T13:44:00Z — 2027-04-10T13:52:00Z (peak) with tailing elevated latencies through 14:05Z.

Actions taken so far:
- Applied a hotfix to the autoscaler config to stop aggressive ramp-downs (Connor).
- Added pre-warming for GPU instance types for model variants impacted (Lauren coordinating infra).
- Collected traces and saved artifacts to the FluxBank incident folder.

Planned next steps: finish the detailed timeline, craft a customer-facing RCA, and propose mitigation sprints (4/12–4/23). I will own the external summary to FluxBank.

—Marissa

[Note: do not include internal debug logs in the customer message; only distilled evidence and commitments.]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <ops@fluxbank.com>, Priya Raman <priya.r@fluxbank.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-15T09:00:00Z
Subject: Post-incident summary and committed mitigations for April 10 event

Oliver / Priya —

Thank you again for your patience while we completed the investigation. Below is a concise, evidence-based summary of the April 10 event, our findings, and the specific mitigations Redwood is committing to. If you'd prefer a walkthrough, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week.

Executive summary:
- What happened: A combination of an autoscaler regression and increased cold-start latency on a subset of GPU instances caused a temporary under-provisioning of inference capacity. Result: elevated latencies and intermittent 503s for a small portion of FluxBank traffic between 13:44–13:52 UTC.
- Customer impact: Estimated ~6% request failure rate during the peak; retry logic in your client recovered most requests, but we recognize this disrupted real-time product flows.
- Current status: All hotfixes are in place; no related incidents observed on subsequent replay windows.

Root cause (evidence):
- Controller logs: autoscaler invoked ramp-down path at 13:44:03 despite sustained queue growth (see attached timeline).
- Trace samples: requests that landed on freshly provisioned nodes experienced ~350ms additional cold-start time due to a kernel-level interaction on the GPU images that was introduced in a provider-managed update on 2027-04-09.
- Combined effect: delayed capacity replenishment during the traffic burst; queueing caused transient 503s when request buffers hit per-process limits.

Action items and timeline (committed):
1) Immediate/hotfix (complete) — 4/10
   - Reverted the aggressive ramp-down rule in the autoscaler (done).
   - Enabled pre-warming hooks for the impacted instance family (done).
   - Captured and shared traces and the incident CSV (attached: fluxbank_incident_timeline.csv).
2) Short-term (by 4/23) — engineering sprint
   - Add guardrails to autoscaler to consider persistent queue growth windows before deprovisioning.
   - Add an anomaly alert for cold-start pattern changes tied to kernel/provider updates.
   - Run a mini chaos test to validate pre-warm behavior under burst traffic.
3) Medium-term (by 5/14) — platform improvements
   - Tighter integration between kernel/AMI change detection and our model-serving pre-warm logic.
   - Improved instrumentation: per-route cold-start histograms and a customer-facing latency dashboard.

Compensation and next steps:
- We propose a one-time commercial credit equivalent to two days of peak usage for April 10. If that is acceptable, we’ll route the request through your account lead and finance.
- Offer: a joint review session to walk through the timeline and validate the proposed mitigations (we can run the test plan in a staging window).

Attachments: fluxbank_incident_timeline.csv, fluxbank_rca_summary.pdf, mitigation-plan.xlsx

Please let me know if you'd like any additional evidence (raw traces) or prefer a call to review. We apologize for the disruption and are committed to preventing recurrence.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the detailed write-up and the attachments. A couple quick items from our side: 
- We accept the proposed credit — we'll route through procurement and loop you in.
- Can you confirm whether the pre-warm hooks will add any additional cost to our reserved pool? We need to understand billing impact.
- We would like to schedule the joint review on Thursday 4/22 at 15:00 UTC if that works for your team.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Thanks,
Priya
Head of Platform Reliability, FluxBank
